newsitem.title: UK: Brady tone positive, eye on Brazil, Venezuela bonds.
newsitem.headline: Brady tone positive, eye on Brazil, Venezuela bonds.

text.p: Emerging market debt was marginally firmer across-the-board in limited trade on Friday as players held back from taking big positions ahead of the weekend, dealers said.

"We're up about 1/8 of a point across-the-board this morning," a dealer at a U.S. bank said. "The tone is positive for today and there is no significant news, so most of trade is just U.S. Treasury driven."
"Emerging market debt has generally remained firm over the course of the past week," ANZ Investment Bank said in its weekly emering market debt commentary.
"Bulgaria, Ecuador and Venezuela have lead the way," it added.
Dealers said the focus was also on Brazil, amid its global issue/Brady exchange and Venezuela upcoming Eurobond.
Brazil's $1.0 billion global bond is being issued as part of a Brazilian effort to swap or buy back Brady bonds. The offer will expire June 3 unless extended or ended earlier by Brazil.
Price talk now among dealers and investors pegged the global at about 375-385 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
Meanwhile Venezuela plans to set $315 million 10-year Eurobond via ING Barings.
Price talk for the bond is inside of 300 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries.
"Certainly Brazil and Venezuela were the best performers this week," a dealer said. "But now that Brazil has had a good run-up there might be some profit-taking."

Brady bond experts also said market participants would again start to look to key U.S. economic data to assess what the Federal Reserve's move might be at the next Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting in July. -- Hayley Pienaar, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7718
